Traditional Twelfth Night Roasted Meat

Served at: Twelfth Night

Serves 6Prep 15 minCook 1 hr 30 min

Roasted meat is a classic centerpiece for Twelfth Night celebrations, marking the end of the Christmas season and the arrival of Epiphany. This hearty dish symbolizes abundance and festivity, often served with seasonal vegetables and rich gravies to warm the winter gathering.

Ingredients

  • 4 lb (1.8 kg) beef roast or leg of lamb
  • 2 tbsp (30 ml) olive oil
  • 4 cloves garlic, minced
  • 1 tbsp (15 ml) fresh rosemary, chopped
  • 1 tbsp (15 ml) fresh thyme, chopped
  • 1 tsp (5 ml) salt
  • 1/2 tsp (2.5 ml) black pepper
  • 1 cup (240 ml) beef broth or red wine
  • 2 large onions, quartered
  • 4 carrots, cut into chunks
  • 3 stalks celery, cut into chunks

Method

  1. Preheat the oven to 375°F (190°C).
  2. In a small bowl, mix olive oil, minced garlic, rosemary, thyme, salt, and pepper.
  3. Rub the herb mixture all over the meat, ensuring even coverage.
  4. Place the onions, carrots, and celery in the bottom of a roasting pan to create a bed for the meat.
  5. Set the meat on top of the vegetables in the roasting pan.
  6. Pour the beef broth or red wine into the pan to keep the meat moist during roasting.
  7. Roast the meat in the preheated oven for about 1 hour and 30 minutes, or until a meat thermometer reads 135°F (57°C) for medium-rare or 145°F (63°C) for medium.
  8. Baste the meat occasionally with pan juices to enhance flavor and moisture.
  9. Remove the meat from the oven and let it rest for 15 minutes before slicing.
  10. Serve sliced roasted meat with the roasted vegetables and pan gravy.

Tips

  • Use a meat thermometer to ensure perfect doneness.
  • For a festive touch, add dried fruits like prunes or apricots to the roasting pan.
  • Leftover roasted meat can be used in hearty stews or sandwiches.
